correctness.rationale: For each changed man, strict men-optimality forces a one-unit-or-greater utility decline, making his utility ratio at most (n-1)/n. Each of the same number of changed women has ratio at most n. Multiplying gives (n-1)^k; cyclic top-ranked-men/ top-ranked-women witnesses attain the bound for every moved-set size. Equality with n>=3 requires all n pairs to change and equality in every factor, giving the exact first/second and first/last rank pattern and n!D_n((n-2)!)^(2n) distinct preference profiles. For n=2 the bound implies equal Nash welfare of every stable matching. Independently constructed exact integer brute enumeration checks all 16 and 46656 profiles at n=2 and n=3, and witnesses n<=14; finite checks are not extrapolated to prove the theorem.

value.rationale: A newly studied fair-stable-marriage objective motivates asking the worst-case cost of retaining the conventional proposing-side mechanism instead of optimizing Nash welfare. The exact sharp, unbounded sqrt(n-1) efficiency loss quantitatively distinguishes mechanisms; all-n equality rigidity and precise derangement enumeration identify the profiles responsible rather than a routine restatement of proposer-optimality. Exact minimax behavior for n=2 is a meaningful boundary. Scope restrictions to positive rank utilities are explicit.
